title: SessionStarted
description: The session is open and its engine has initialised. Normalised by the adapter of the engine — the engine's own message is never emitted raw (ADR-006, ADR-025).

workspacePath.description: The workspace the session runs in, already normalised and already inside the allowlist.

permissionMode.description: The canonical mode (plan 28, D-16): `ask` — every call that needs leave asks; `acceptEdits` — file edits are accepted, the rest asks; `readOnly` — nothing changes: the server refuses every write and every shell, whatever the engine thinks; `allowAll` — Permitir tudo, ours: the server allows every call no rule refuses, but questions and plans (ADR-022). Only the modes the engine announces in `capabilities.permissionModes` are offered. The previous protocol named them `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan` and `allowAll`, and its `bypassPermissions` is refused.

engine.description: The engine the session runs on — an `id` of `GET /engines`, whose `displayName` is how a screen names it. The client never decides by it.

conversation.description: The conversation the session is: what `GET /transcripts/:engine/:id/messages` reads, and what a later `session.start` takes as `resumeFrom`. Equal to `resumedFrom` when one of our own conversations is continued in place; new when a conversation begun elsewhere is forked.

resumedFrom.description: The conversation this session continues, when it is a resume. Absent for a fresh session. The history before the first turn of this session is read from it, over HTTP — the replay buffer only ever holds what this session said.

capabilities.description: What this session can do. The client hides what it cannot.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks for the life of the session, when one was chosen — by the client, a folder's default or the user's. Absent for the model's own default.

outputStyle.description: The output style the session was opened with, when a default chose one. Absent for the installation's.

defaultsFrom.description: Where the model the session runs with came from: what the client sent in `session.start`, the default of the nearest folder, the user's default, or the installation's — a default that went stale falls back to it (plan 13, B-15).
